# isRichTextValue

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a rich text value.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isRichTextValue() — Checks whether a value is a rich text value. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isRichTextValue(value: unknown): value is GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.RichTextValue;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "RichTextValue"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a rich text value; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.RichTextValue` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const value = SpreadsheetApp.newRichTextValue().setText("a").build();

isRichTextValue(value); // => true
isRichTextValue({}); // => false
isRichTextValue(null); // => false
```
